In front, back, left and right views the outline is a single upright figure with coat hem, arms and feet in place, and nothing sticks out or is missing. The side-view outline matches the front-view proportions.

M2.reason: Measured size 33.3 x 21.7 x 68 against the asked height of 68 (offset 0%), so the height is within 15% of the brief's size.

M3.reason: Parts the brief names, checked down to small ones: white lab coat with lapels and open front, blue shirt collar, red patterned tie, belt, light trousers, glasses (frames visible in the front and three-quarter views), bald crown with grey hair at the sides and back (back and back-left views), hands, and brown shoes. Each is present once in the right place; none is missing or doubled.

M4.reason: Regions read as the brief asks: white coat and trousers, blue shirt, red-and-dark patterned tie, pink skin on the head and hands, brown shoes, dark belt. The colours hold steady across all ten views with no region drifting to another colour.

M5.reason: Surface detail is there at a sharpness that suits the game: tie pattern, shirt collar seam, coat folds at the sleeves and hem, glasses rims, and grey hair texture. Nothing smeared or missing in the front and three-quarter views.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test, which is measured apart. In the line-up the asset was never picked as the one not made by Valve (the judges picked C, D, D, A where it stood at D, B, C, C), so it passed for one of the game's in all four readings.

M7.reason: The front view is the front: face and tie to the camera, figure upright. In the side and motion views the feet sit on the same floor line, so it stands on its origin as a Valve scientist does.

M8.reason: Triangles 740, under twice the median of Half-Life's people (2 x 504 = 1008) and under their third quartile for its kind. The SMAK check reports no errors. Nothing a player can see is open: the top and below views show only the body's outer surface, and the open underside of the trousers and coat in the below view is not visible in play.

C1.reason: Motion frames 0/18 to 18/18 show the run: arms swing opposite the legs, the feet alternate off and on the floor line, and the coat and hair stay with the body through every frame. Nothing comes apart, sinks or floats. The walk in the side and back-right views is consistent with the run.
